name: optimize_python_repeated_max_extraction
description: O(n^2) max()+remove() per extraction -> one descending sort; budget calibrated (naive ~6.5s native at n=50k vs ~0.005s, budget 2s)
prompts: ranking(scores, k) in leaderboard.py returns the k highest scores in descending order (k may be as large as the whole list). It currently extracts one maximum per iteration with max() followed by list.remove() - two linear scans per extraction, O(n^2) overall and far too slow for a full ranking of tens of thousands of scores. Rewrite it to sort once (descending) and slice, returning exactly the same list for every input - duplicates each appear, k larger than the input returns everything, and the input list must not be mutated. Keep the function name and signature.

setup_files.leaderboard.py:
def ranking(scores, k):
    """The k highest scores in descending order (k may equal len(scores))."""
    remaining = list(scores)
    out = []
    for _ in range(min(k, len(remaining))):
        best = max(remaining)
        remaining.remove(best)
        out.append(best)
    return out

test_setup_files.test_leaderboard.py:
import random
import time

from leaderboard import ranking


def test_basic_ranking():
    assert ranking([10, 50, 20, 40], 3) == [50, 40, 20]


def test_full_ranking_with_duplicates():
    assert ranking([5, 1, 5, 3], 4) == [5, 5, 3, 1]


def test_k_larger_than_input_and_empty():
    assert ranking([7, 2], 10) == [7, 2]
    assert ranking([], 3) == []


def test_input_not_mutated():
    scores = [3, 1, 2]
    ranking(scores, 2)
    assert scores == [3, 1, 2]


def test_performance_full_ranking():
    random.seed(3)
    n = 50000
    scores = [random.randrange(0, 10**6) for _ in range(n)]
    expected_head = sorted(scores, reverse=True)[:3]

    start = time.perf_counter()
    got = ranking(scores, n)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    assert len(got) == n
    assert got[:3] == expected_head
    assert got[-1] == min(scores)
    # calibrated: max()+remove() per extraction is ~6.5s on fast native
    # hardware and slower in the sandbox; a single sort is ~0.005s
    assert elapsed < 2.0, (
        f"ranking took {elapsed:.2f}s for {n} scores; expected one sort "
        f"(sorted(..., reverse=True)[:k]), not max()+list.remove() per "
        f"extraction, which is O(n^2)"
    )
